chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn Sakun, from Abdullah ibn Waddah, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The price of the 'adhrah of the sea-cow (or whale) is [permissible]. For this report is interpreted as referring to the 'adhrah of humans, and the first [report] is interpreted as referring to the 'adhrah of animals such as camels, cattle, and sheep. There is no contradiction between the two reports, and that which reveals what we mentioned.

key_terms.اَلسُّحْت: The sea-cow or whale, a marine animal discussed in Shia jurisprudence regarding its permissibility and parts.
key_terms.اَلْخَبَر: The report or narration, referring to the hadith text being interpreted.
key_terms.اَلْعَذِرَة: The 'adhrah, a specific part of an animal (often the udder or a fatty portion) used in discussions of ritual purity and price.
key_terms.مَحْمُولٌ عَلَى: Interpreted as referring to / carried upon (a technical term in hadith criticism for resolving apparent contradictions by assigning different contexts).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the 'adhrah of the sea-cow (suh't) and how does it relate to the 'adhrah of livestock?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the permissibility of consuming the 'adhrah (a specific fatty or edible part) of the 'suh't (sea-cow/whale). The scholar resolves the apparent contradiction with other narrations by distinguishing between the 'adhrah of humans and that of livestock, demonstrating the nuanced application of *ta'wil* (interpretation) in Shia fiqh to harmonize seemingly conflicting reports.
